description:
Jordan Staal capped a legendary 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs by capturing the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP. The Hurricanes captain scored eight goals in the postseason, including a historic six in the Final against Vegas — becoming the first player in more than 50 years to score in each of the first five games of a Stanley Cup Final and just the second team captain in 105 years to reach six goals in the series.

In Game 2, Staal delivered a crucial third-period goal that helped fuel Carolina’s resilience. In Game 4, he scored twice, with his second of the night — a desperate, swat of the puck from in tight — proving to be the game-winner and producing one of the series’ most iconic moments. In Game 5, he tied the game with a first-period tip-in, continuing his streak. 

Beyond the goals, Staal dominated the faceoff circle throughout the Final, winning 68 percent of his draws (83 wins against just 39 losses) while matching up against Vegas’ top centers and anchoring a lockdown defensive effort. The veteran’s combination of clutch scoring, leadership, and two-way excellence powered Carolina to its first championship since 2006 and cemented his place in franchise lore.
